text:
sanjay: Heads-up — canary apply of the gpufleet module split just failed during hook stage. Seeing tainted node sets and a bunch of AZ-affinity probes failing.

maya: ugh. Which hook? the kube taint/untaint hook?

sanjay: yes, hook: `scripts/rollout/mark-gpupool-ready.sh` — it timed out waiting for nodes in az-b to join. deploy-bot reported hook timeout.

infra-bot: Canary rollout: gpufleet-v2 (module-split) failed at hook_step 3 — timeout 1800s, reverting canary.

eli: Do we know root cause? module split changed provider alias usage in gpupool -> vpc module? Could be provider alias mismatch causing resources to be created in wrong region/az.

adrian: I looked at the TF plan earlier. The new gpupool module drops `provider = aws.eu-west-1` alias and expects the root provider; the vpc module still references `provider = aws.eu-west-1`. When gitops applied, lockfile had provider v4.x vs v5.x mismatch.

sanjay: exact errors in k8s logs: `failed to label node: AccessDenied kms:Encrypt` for node bootstrap, and `InvalidProviderConfiguration: provider alias not found` for subnet attach.

maya: KMS error suggests the IAM changes in the split included a new KMS key alias `alias/gpufleet-v2` but canary cluster still uses old alias. Did we run the kms migration script?

eli: Not before canary. The module Split PR included the KMS alias resource but we didn't include the migration TF-runset to populated the alias in all regions. That explains the bootstrap failure (node bootstrapping needs to decrypt userdata).

adrian: Also noticed autoscaler thrash: nodes come up in az-a, but scheduler forces pods into az-b because node labels mismatched. Inter-AZ traffic spiked — cost alarm fired.

sanjay: Actions I propose: 1) pause rollout, 2) revert provider alias changes in canary branch, 3) run idempotent migration job to create KMS alias and IAM role bindings, 4) re-run canary with extended hook timeout and a readiness probe that checks node KMS decrypt.

maya: +1. Also we should add a gitops preflight check that validates provider aliases exist in the state lockfile and that `.terraform.lock.hcl` provider checksums match expected. A quick script: 
```
# verify provider alias present
terraform providers | grep aws || exit 1
# verify lockfile
shasum -a256 .terraform.lock.hcl | grep <expected> || echo "lockfile mismatch"
```

eli: Can we do a safer rollout pattern: create alias objects (KMS, IAM roles) in a separate migration plan that can be promoted before module changes? That way applies don't rely on ordering inside the same PR.

adrian: Agreed. Also add a post-apply smoke test that attempts to decrypt a test blob with the new alias and performs a kube bootstrap dry-run. Hook should fail fast if decrypt fails.

sanjay: I'll push a revert for the provider alias lines and open a follow-up PR with a migration-only plan + extended smoke tests. I'll also tag @maya and @eli in the PR for review.

infra-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-6382 "gpufleet module-split canary failure: provider alias & kms migration" — assigned to sanjay.

maya: For the longer term: add CI gate to ensure modules that touch KMS/IAM publish a migration guide with a terraform plan snippet and a lockfile checksum.

eli: Also let's add a `gitops/preflight` job to the pipeline that runs the provider-alias detection and a lightweight `terraform plan -target=module.kms -out=migrate.tfplan` to surface surprises.

adrian: I'll squash a small helm chart tweak to the taint hook so it tolerates transient decrypt errors and retries with backoff.

sanjay: ok locking the canary branch now. Will post updates here once revert and migration plan are live. Sorry for the blast during sprint prep :grimacing:

maya: Thanks for fast triage everyone :thumbsup:
